groups.description: Crop and livestock statistics, physical commodity prices, and trade flows. The interesting property of this group is the estimate-then-settle pattern: a production forecast is issued monthly, revised monthly, and eventually replaced by a survey. That is a correction-latency dimension with a real anchor at the end of it, which few other domains offer.

entries.name: USDA NASS Quick Stats
entries.why: Census and survey estimates for every US crop, with survey results superseding forecasts.

entries.name: USDA Economic Research Service Data
entries.why: Farm income and food price outlook series, revised on a published calendar.

entries.name: USDA FAS Production, Supply and Distribution
entries.why: Global balance sheets by commodity, which FAO and traders both republish downstream.

entries.name: USDA FAS Export Sales Reporting
entries.why: Weekly export sales on a fixed Thursday release, so a late file is visible immediately.

entries.name: USDA AMS Market News
entries.why: Physical cash prices for produce, meat, and grain, reported several times a day.

entries.name: USDA WASDE
entries.why: The monthly estimate that moves grain markets, with every prior month restated beside it.

entries.name: USDA Cropland Data Layer
entries.why: Annual land cover raster, reissued with method changes that a schema-stability test catches.

entries.name: FAO FAOSTAT
entries.why: The global reference series, largely derivative of national statistics offices.

entries.name: FAO AQUASTAT
entries.why: Water use by country and sector, sparse enough to exercise completeness by segment.

entries.name: FAO FishStat
entries.why: Capture and aquaculture production, a domain no other registry entry covers.

entries.name: AMIS Market Database
entries.why: A G20 aggregation of USDA, FAO, and national numbers, so lineage is the whole product.

entries.name: FEWS NET
entries.why: Food security classifications on a scheduled outlook, with revisions between releases.

entries.name: UN Comtrade
entries.why: Bilateral trade flows where each pair is reported twice and rarely agrees, which is a built-in internal consistency test.

entries.name: WTO Timeseries
entries.why: Tariff and trade indicators, derivative of member notifications with long lags.

entries.name: ITC Trade Map
entries.why: A Comtrade derivative with its own estimates filled in, which makes the lineage visible.

entries.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries
entries.why: Annual production and reserves per mineral, with estimates flagged as such in the source.

entries.name: OPEC Reference Basket Price
entries.why: One daily number with a named formula, which is the simplest possible reproducibility test.

entries.name: CME Group Daily Settlements
entries.why: Public settlement files anchor the cash prices elsewhere in this group. Terms need a careful read before anything is routed, because exchange data is licensed aggressively.

entries.name: ICE Public Reports
entries.why: A second exchange publishing settlements, which gives CME a cross-venue comparison.

entries.name: LME Official Prices
entries.reason: LME price data is sold under a market data licence with per-user reporting obligations. Redistribution through a router is exactly what that licence prices, so this is a customer-credentials case at best, and not before Phase 2.
entries.why: The metals benchmark. Named here so nobody researches the licence a second time.

groups.description: Agricultural reporting, food prices, and trade statistics. What distinguishes this group is that the release instant has direct monetary value, so the gap between publication and availability is not an abstraction. It is also full of mirror publishing: the same crop estimate appears in a national release, an international database, and a market newsletter, each with a different vintage and none citing the others. Candidates only, terms unread.

entries.name: USDA FAS Global Agricultural Trade System
entries.why: Trade flows that Comtrade also carries, with a different revision schedule.

entries.name: USDA FAS Production Estimates
entries.why: US estimates of foreign crops that frequently disagree with the national statistics offices in this registry.

entries.name: USDA ERS Food Price Outlook
entries.why: A forecast revised monthly, so its error is measurable against the CPI series we already route to.

entries.name: USDA RMA Crop Insurance Data
entries.why: Indemnity data restated for years as claims settle, a slow correction case.

entries.name: USDA FSA Crop Acreage Reports
entries.why: Administrative acreage that differs from the survey-based NASS figures, a definitional disagreement worth surfacing.

entries.name: USDA AMS Livestock Mandatory Reporting
entries.why: Reports published several times daily, with confidentiality suppression built into the rule rather than the data.

entries.name: USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer API
entries.why: The query interface over the CropScape entry already registered, published annually.

entries.name: FAO GAEZ Agro-Ecological Zones
entries.why: Modelled potential rather than observed output, which the envelope must not conflate with a measurement.

entries.name: FAO Food Price Index
entries.why: A monthly index with a fixed release day that news outlets republish within minutes, which makes lag visible to anyone watching.

entries.name: FAO GIEWS Country Briefs
entries.why: Early warning assessments in narrative form, which belongs in untrusted_text.

entries.name: FAO Food Price Monitoring and Analysis Tool
entries.why: Domestic market prices collected from national sources, a deep and poorly documented lineage chain.

entries.name: WFP VAM Food Prices
entries.why: Market-level prices in places where no statistics office publishes, which is real coverage rather than duplication.

entries.name: IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis
entries.why: Classification decisions with a published method and periodic revision, which is a graded output produced by someone else, exactly as ADR-0014 prefers.

entries.name: AMIS Policy Database
entries.why: Export restrictions announced by governments, a change feed with immediate price effects.

entries.name: International Grains Council Market Report
entries.why: Partly free and partly subscription, so one source spans two use classes.

entries.name: ABARES Agricultural Commodities
entries.why: Quarterly forecasts from a major exporter, revised each quarter.

entries.name: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada Outlook
entries.why: Another exporter forecast on the same crops, which makes disagreement measurable.

entries.name: CONAB Crop Bulletin (Brazil)
entries.why: The national estimate that USDA's foreign estimate competes with, which is the single clearest published disagreement in the commodity world.

entries.name: Bolsa de Cereales Weekly Crop Report (Argentina)
entries.why: A private exchange whose weekly estimate moves markets before any official figure.

entries.name: JRC MARS Crop Monitoring
entries.why: European yield forecasts derived from satellite and weather inputs already in this registry.

entries.name: EU Agri-food Data Portal
entries.why: Weekly price series for the whole union, published under one licence.

entries.name: EU Milk Market Observatory
entries.why: Member states report on different schedules, which is completeness by segment in practice.

entries.name: EU Meat Market Observatory
entries.why: The same structure on a different commodity, so one adapter covers both.

entries.name: Defra Farming Statistics (UK)
entries.why: National statistics with a pre-announced release calendar to score punctuality against.

entries.name: AgMIP Model Intercomparison Data
entries.why: Multiple models on one question, which is disagreement published deliberately.

entries.name: CGIAR Genebank Platform Data
entries.why: Accession records with international treaty terms attached to use, an unusual licence shape.

entries.name: Genesys Plant Genetic Resources
entries.why: Aggregates genebank holdings worldwide, with provenance fields already present.

entries.name: WOAH WAHIS Animal Disease Notifications
entries.why: Outbreak notifications trigger immediate trade bans, so the value of a minute of freshness is quantifiable here.

entries.name: EPPO Global Database
entries.why: Plant pest reports with per-country status changes, a natural change feed.

entries.name: IPPC Official Pest Reports
entries.why: Country notifications that EPPO also republishes, giving another lineage pair.

entries.name: ITC Market Access Map
entries.why: Applied tariffs, which are the rules behind the trade flows already registered.

entries.name: WTO Tariff Download Facility
entries.why: Bound and applied rates from a second publisher, which lets the two be reconciled.

entries.name: EU TARIC Database
entries.why: Daily legal updates to tariff codes, which is a genuine change feed with legal force.

entries.name: USITC DataWeb
entries.why: US trade statistics revised monthly, with the revision published as its own release.

entries.name: Census International Trade API
entries.why: The primary that USITC DataWeb republishes, which completes a domestic lineage pair.

groups.description: Aviation and maritime movement data, plus the regulators that publish the reference data behind it. Two things make this group unusual. The positional feeds are crowd-sourced as often as they are official, so the primary is frequently a volunteer network rather than an authority; and the commercial terms are strict enough that several entries here will never be promotable under H3. Recording that is the point. Candidates only, terms unread.

entries.name: FAA Aviation System Performance Metrics
entries.why: Official delay causes, which would anchor any accuracy claim about a commercial flight tracker.

entries.name: FAA National Airspace System Resources
entries.why: The 28-day airspace cycle is a published revision schedule, which is a free test of punctuality scoring.

entries.name: FAA NOTAM Service
entries.why: Safety-critical text notices, which belong in untrusted_text rather than anywhere near a prompt.

entries.name: FAA ADS-B Performance Reports
entries.why: Coverage statistics that would explain gaps in the crowd-sourced networks below.

entries.name: BTS On-Time Performance
entries.why: The settled monthly record every realtime flight feed can be graded against, which is what an anchor means under H1.

entries.name: EUROCONTROL Aviation Data
entries.why: European traffic and delay data with a stated reuse policy.

entries.name: EASA Safety Publications
entries.why: Airworthiness directives with effective dates, a natural change feed.

entries.name: NTSB Aviation Accident Database
entries.why: Records are amended for years after the event, which is the correction latency dimension in an unusually pure form.

entries.name: ICAO Data Services
entries.why: Authoritative but commercially licensed, so it can only ever be pass-through.

entries.name: OpenSky Network REST API
entries.why: The REST interface behind the OpenSky entry already registered, and a clear case where the free endpoint and the pro endpoint must route differently.

entries.name: ADS-B Exchange
entries.why: Unfiltered coverage that the other networks deliberately restrict, which makes it a disagreement source rather than a duplicate.

entries.name: adsbdb Aircraft Database
entries.why: Reference data that positional feeds join against, so its staleness propagates invisibly.

entries.name: National Aircraft Registries Index
entries.why: Registries outside the US publish on wildly different clocks, which is a completeness story worth telling.

entries.name: EUROCONTROL R&D Data Archive
entries.why: Historical trajectories released for research only, a use-class routing example.

entries.name: OurAirports
entries.why: Community-maintained airport reference data in the public domain, which makes it an easy early promotion target.

entries.name: Aviation Edge
entries.why: A commercial aggregator, listed so the registry records what we deliberately do not redistribute.

entries.name: FlightAware AeroAPI
entries.why: Pass-through only, and a good test of whether the customer's own key really stays theirs.

entries.name: NOAA Electronic Navigational Charts
entries.why: Weekly chart corrections with a published notice cycle.

entries.name: USACE Lock Performance Monitoring
entries.why: Inland waterway throughput, a supply chain signal with a single publisher.

entries.name: USACE Waterborne Commerce Statistics
entries.why: Published with a long lag, which the freshness dimension should state plainly rather than penalise as an outage.

entries.name: MarineCadastre AIS Vessel Traffic
entries.why: Free historical AIS in the public domain, which is the anchor against which commercial realtime vessel feeds could be graded.

entries.name: AISHub
entries.why: Data sharing is reciprocal rather than open, an unusual licence shape worth modelling.

entries.name: EMSA SafeSeaNet Public Reports
entries.why: European port call statistics with no free realtime equivalent.

entries.name: IMO GISIS
entries.why: Ship particulars behind a registration, so it can only be pass-through.

entries.name: Paris MOU Port State Control Inspections
entries.why: Detention records that are corrected after appeals, a correction latency case.

entries.name: Tokyo MOU Port State Control
entries.why: The Asian counterpart, which lets two regimes be compared on the same vessel.

entries.name: Global Port Call Statistics (UNCTAD)
entries.why: A derived global series built from AIS, so its lineage runs through a commercial vendor.

entries.name: Panama Canal Authority Transit Statistics
entries.why: Draft restrictions during drought years made this a closely watched series with one publisher.

entries.name: Suez Canal Authority Traffic Statistics
entries.why: Monthly transits, widely cited and rarely versioned.

entries.name: NOAA Tide Predictions
entries.why: Predictions rather than observations, which forces the envelope to distinguish the two.

entries.name: NGA Maritime Safety Information
entries.why: Navigational warnings issued continuously, again text that belongs in untrusted_text.

entries.name: VesselFinder API
entries.why: Commercial realtime, listed as pass-through only.

entries.name: Global Fishing Watch API
entries.why: Openly licensed for non-commercial use with a clear terms page, which makes it a good demonstration of use-class routing.

entries.name: ICOADS Marine Observations
entries.why: A century of ship weather observations, and one of the longest-running revision histories in any science dataset.

entries.name: Argo Float Profiles
entries.why: Real-time and delayed-mode versions of the same profile are both published, which is revision behaviour made explicit by design.

entries.name: EMODnet Physics
entries.why: European marine observations aggregated from national networks, a deep lineage chain.

entries.name: IOC Sea Level Station Monitoring
entries.why: Minute-resolution gauges whose outages are visible immediately, a fast freshness signal.

entries.name: Permanent Service for Mean Sea Level
entries.why: The slow, curated counterpart to the realtime gauges, which is the same measurement on a different clock.

entries.name: Port of Los Angeles Signal
entries.why: Forward-looking container volumes published weekly, which is a rare forecast with a named publisher.

entries.name: Port of Rotterdam Open Data
entries.why: Europe's largest port publishing selected operational data directly.

groups.description: Central banks and monetary authorities. These are the cleanest primaries in the registry: a policy rate has one publisher, the publication instant is recorded to the minute, and every aggregator downstream is provably a derivative. That makes the group the best available test bed for freshness lag and for lineage inference. Candidates only, terms unread.

entries.name: ECB Data Portal
entries.why: SDMX over the euro area's reference rates and monetary aggregates, and the primary behind the exchange-rate feeds already registered.

entries.name: Federal Reserve H.15 Selected Interest Rates
entries.why: FRED republishes this; holding both lets us show a republisher's lag against its own upstream.

entries.name: Federal Reserve Data Download Program
entries.why: The machine interface for every Fed statistical release, including revision vintages.

entries.name: New York Fed Markets Data
entries.why: SOFR and repo operations published same-day with an explicit revision flag, which is the revision dimension handed to us.

entries.name: Bank of Japan Time-Series Data Search
entries.why: Japanese monetary primary with long history, needed for any as_of replay before 2000.

entries.name: People's Bank of China Statistics
entries.why: The only primary for Chinese monetary aggregates, republished everywhere with lag.

entries.name: Reserve Bank of India Database on Indian Economy
entries.why: Weekly statistical supplement with a stable structure, which is unusually good for diffing.

entries.name: Banco Central do Brasil SGS
entries.why: A well-documented open API over thousands of Brazilian series, no key required.

entries.name: Banco de Mexico SIE
entries.why: Keyed REST API with documented series identifiers and same-day FX fixes.

entries.name: Banco Central de la Republica Argentina
entries.why: Official rates that diverge sharply from parallel-market references, which is a disagreement worth reporting rather than resolving.

entries.name: Bank of Canada Valet API
entries.why: One of the best-documented open central bank APIs anywhere, with an explicit terms page, so it is a strong early promotion candidate.

entries.name: Reserve Bank of Australia Statistical Tables
entries.why: Spreadsheet releases on a fixed schedule, a good test of the file-feed adapter.

entries.name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Statistics
entries.why: Small, punctual publisher useful as a freshness control.

entries.name: Swiss National Bank Data Portal
entries.why: Serves csv and json with explicit dataset versions.

entries.name: Sveriges Riksbank Swea API
entries.why: Publishes rates through a documented REST API with an OpenAPI description.

entries.name: Norges Bank API
entries.why: SDMX exchange rates with a clear licence statement.

entries.name: Danmarks Nationalbank Statbank
entries.why: Shares the PxWeb shape used by the Nordic statistics offices, so the adapter is reused.

entries.name: Deutsche Bundesbank Time Series Database
entries.why: National euro-area primary whose series the ECB also carries, a ready lineage pair.

entries.name: Banque de France Webstat
entries.why: Second euro-area national primary, keyed but documented.

entries.name: Banca d'Italia Statistical Database
entries.why: Completes the large euro-area national set for lineage work.

entries.name: Banco de Espana Statistical Bulletin
entries.why: Publishes bulletin tables on a fixed calendar, easy to score for punctuality.

entries.name: De Nederlandsche Bank Statistics
entries.why: Pension and insurance aggregates that the ECB reports only partially.

entries.name: Bank for International Settlements Statistics
entries.why: The cross-border banking derivative built from the national banks in this file, which is lineage depth of two.

entries.name: CBRT EVDS (Turkey)
entries.why: Keyed API over a monetary series set that moves fast enough to make caching decisions visible.

entries.name: South African Reserve Bank Data Portal
entries.why: The African monetary primary with the longest continuous published history.

entries.name: Central Bank of Nigeria Statistics
entries.why: Multiple official FX windows have coexisted here, so one question can have several correct answers, which is what the envelope is for.

entries.name: Central Bank of Kenya Statistics
entries.why: Daily indicative rates published without an API, a scraping-cost example.

entries.name: Bank of Korea ECOS
entries.why: Keyed API with a large series catalogue and stable identifiers.

entries.name: Monetary Authority of Singapore
entries.why: Publishes through the national open data platform with consistent metadata.

entries.name: Hong Kong Monetary Authority Open API
entries.why: A genuine OpenAPI-documented central bank interface, which is still rare.

entries.name: Central Bank of the UAE Statistics
entries.why: Gulf monetary primary with pegged-rate series the aggregators treat as constant.

entries.name: Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) Statistics
entries.why: Monthly bulletin containing reserve data that moves oil markets.

entries.name: Bank of Russia Statistics
entries.why: Sanctions have changed what is published and when, which is a completeness history worth capturing rather than an argument for ignoring it.

entries.name: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Statistics
entries.why: Remittance series that nothing else publishes first.

entries.name: Bank Negara Malaysia Open API
entries.why: A versioned public API with an explicit content negotiation scheme, which is a schema stability example done right.

groups.description: Sanctions lists, procurement, lobbying, campaign finance, and political event data. Sanctions lists are the one group in the registry where staleness is a compliance failure rather than an inconvenience, which makes freshness lag the dimension that matters most and the one a caller would actually pay to have measured. Most of the rest is derivative of filings that are already elsewhere in the registry, which makes the group a good lineage exhibit.

entries.name: OFAC Sanctions Lists
entries.why: The list where an hour of staleness is a compliance problem, which is the strongest argument for a freshness-lag number that anyone outside this project will recognise.

entries.name: EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List
entries.why: The same designations as OFAC with different timing, so disagreement is real and dateable.

entries.name: UK OFSI Consolidated List
entries.why: A third list covering overlapping entities, which makes a three-way compare meaningful.

entries.name: UN Security Council Consolidated List
entries.why: The upstream that national lists implement, so the lag between them is the lineage.

entries.name: World Bank Debarred Firms
entries.why: Exclusions with start and end dates, so an expired entry that lingers is a visible error.

entries.name: Open Ownership Register
entries.why: Beneficial ownership in a standard schema, collected from registers of uneven quality.

entries.name: Tenders Electronic Daily
entries.why: EU tender notices published daily with corrigenda, which is correction latency in public.

entries.name: Contracts Finder
entries.why: UK notices in OCDS, the same schema as TED, so a cross-country compare is cheap.

entries.name: SAM.gov Entity and Exclusions
entries.why: US federal exclusions and entity registrations, joinable to usaspending already in the registry.

entries.name: Senate Lobbying Disclosure
entries.why: Quarterly filings with amendments that supersede, which is our snapshot model exactly.

entries.name: OpenSecrets
entries.why: A derivative of FEC and Senate LDA filings, both of which we already plan to carry.

entries.name: FollowTheMoney
entries.why: State-level campaign finance, the one layer federal sources do not reach.

entries.name: EU Transparency Register
entries.why: Self-declared lobbying data, where internal consistency checks find real contradictions.

entries.name: Open States
entries.why: Fifty state legislatures normalised, with per-state scrapers that fail independently.

entries.name: LegiScan
entries.why: A second read on the same state bills, which makes Open States checkable against a peer.

entries.name: GDELT Project
entries.why: A fifteen-minute event feed built from news text, and therefore the largest untrusted_text surface we would carry. Skeptic review before anything is promoted.

entries.name: ACLED
entries.why: Coded conflict events that are revised retroactively as reports are reconciled.

entries.name: Transparency International CPI
entries.why: A composite of other surveys, published annually, with the source list stated. Lineage.

entries.name: Varieties of Democracy
entries.why: Expert-coded indices with confidence intervals, which no other registry entry carries.

entries.name: Our World in Data
entries.why: Openly derivative of almost everything else here, with the upstream named per chart, which makes it the single best lineage inference test in the registry.

groups.description: Courts, legislation, and legal publishers beyond the entries already registered. Legal data has a property the rest of the registry mostly lacks: the authoritative version is a specific document at a specific moment, and citing the wrong vintage is not a quality issue but an error. That makes as_of replay less of a feature and more of a requirement. Candidates only, terms unread.

entries.name: US Federal Court RSS Docket Feeds
entries.why: Per-court feeds with inconsistent coverage, which is completeness by segment in a domain where gaps matter.

entries.name: Supreme Court of the United States Opinions
entries.why: Slip opinions are later revised into bound volumes, which is an explicit supersession chain.

entries.name: PACER Case Locator
entries.why: Metered per page by the court itself, which is a cost model the envelope would have to report honestly.

entries.name: GovInfo United States Code
entries.why: Annual editions plus continuous amendment, so the current text and the published edition differ.

entries.name: eCFR API
entries.why: Serves the regulation as it stood on any past date, which is as_of replay built into the upstream.

entries.name: State Legislature Bill Feeds Index
entries.why: Fifty publishers with fifty schemas, which is why the LegiScan entry already registered exists and what it costs.

entries.name: Municode Code Library
entries.why: Municipal codes hosted by a private publisher, which raises whether the law itself is redistributable from this copy.

entries.name: American Legal Publishing Code Library
entries.why: A second private host of public ordinances, which makes the question general rather than one vendor's quirk.

entries.name: Open States Bulk Data
entries.why: The bulk counterpart to the Open States API already registered, with a different freshness profile.

entries.name: Court of Justice of the EU Case Law
entries.why: Judgments published in every official language on different days, which is a lag with a language dimension.

entries.name: European Case Law Identifier Search
entries.why: A cross-border identifier scheme, which is the join key national court feeds need.

entries.name: BAILII
entries.why: A charity publishing UK and Irish case law with terms that restrict bulk reuse, which is a hard no under H3 until read.

entries.name: Find Case Law (National Archives UK)
entries.why: An official judgment archive with an explicit open licence and an API, which is the promotable alternative to the scraping-based sources.

entries.name: Legifrance API (France)
entries.why: Consolidated legislation with version dates, which is exactly what a legal as_of needs.

entries.name: Gesetze im Internet (Germany)
entries.why: Bulk XML of federal law, updated continuously without version identifiers, which is a provenance gap we would have to fill ourselves.

entries.name: Rechtspraak.nl Open Data
entries.why: Dutch judgments published openly with ECLI identifiers.

entries.name: Normattiva (Italy)
entries.why: Serves legislation as in force on a chosen date, another upstream that already solved replay.

entries.name: Boletin Oficial del Estado (Spain)
entries.why: A daily official gazette with a documented API, which is a change feed by definition.

entries.name: Canada Gazette
entries.why: Regulatory notices on a fixed weekly schedule.

entries.name: EU Official Journal (EUR-Lex OJ Series)
entries.why: The publication of record for EU law, and the anchor date for anything citing it.

entries.name: AustLII
entries.why: The Australian counterpart to BAILII, with the same reuse question.

entries.name: NZLII
entries.why: Completes the LII family so the licence question can be settled once.

entries.name: Indian Kanoon API
entries.why: A metered private index over public judgments, which is the marketplace model already operating.

entries.name: eCourts Services (India)
entries.why: The official case status system, which is the primary behind several commercial products.

entries.name: International Criminal Court Records
entries.why: Filings released with redaction revisions, which is a correction type nothing else in the registry has.

entries.name: International Court of Justice Case Documents
entries.why: Slow, low-volume, and heavily cited, which is the opposite profile to the docket feeds.

entries.name: WTO Dispute Settlement Database
entries.why: Case status changes drive trade policy, linking this file to the trade entries.

entries.name: ICSID Case Database
entries.why: Investment arbitration records, which are otherwise only available commercially.

entries.name: UNCITRAL Transparency Registry
entries.why: Publishes arbitration documents under a treaty obligation, an unusual licence basis.

entries.name: ECHR HUDOC API
entries.why: The machine interface behind the HUDOC entry already registered.

entries.name: Venice Commission CODICES Database
entries.why: Constitutional case law summarised across jurisdictions, which is a derived layer with a named method.

entries.name: Constitute Project
entries.why: Constitutions tagged by topic with amendment dates, which makes point-in-time queries meaningful.

entries.name: UN Treaty Collection Status
entries.why: Ratification status changes on a slow but irregular clock, which is hard to poll efficiently.

entries.name: SEC Litigation Releases
entries.why: Enforcement actions announced on a daily feed, which pairs with the financial regulators file.

entries.name: DOJ Press Releases and Case Documents
entries.why: Narrative text that must be quarantined, plus structured case identifiers that need not be.

groups.description: Blockchain nodes, indexers, and crypto market data. This group is worth registering for one reason that has nothing to do with crypto as an asset class: it is the only domain where the underlying record is already content-addressed and independently verifiable, so a disagreement between two providers about the same block is unambiguously one provider being wrong. That is the cleanest accuracy anchor available to us anywhere. Candidates only, terms unread.

entries.name: Blockchain.com Data API
entries.why: Long-running public endpoints over Bitcoin chain data, with terms that need reading.

entries.name: Blockchair API
entries.why: Covers many chains through one schema, which is leverage per adapter.

entries.name: mempool.space API
entries.why: Open source and self-hostable, so the same software can be the source and the check on it.

entries.name: Bitcoin Core RPC
entries.why: The reference implementation, which makes it the anchor every indexer above is graded against.

entries.name: Etherscan API
entries.why: The most widely embedded explorer API, with a quota that agents routinely exhaust.

entries.name: Blockscout
entries.why: Open source explorer deployed by many chains, so one adapter reaches dozens of networks.

entries.name: Alchemy Node API
entries.why: Infrastructure sold per request, which is a pass-through candidate with a real cost meter.

entries.name: Infura Node API

entries.name: QuickNode API
entries.why: A third provider, enough for a majority check rather than a coin flip.

entries.name: The Graph Hosted Subgraphs
entries.why: Indexed views whose definitions are themselves versioned code, which is method versioning in the open.

entries.name: Dune Analytics API
entries.why: Query results defined by user-authored SQL, so provenance has to include the query.

entries.name: DefiLlama API
entries.why: Open methodology and a free API, which makes its numbers auditable in a way most of this domain is not.

entries.name: CoinMarketCap API
entries.why: A widely cited aggregate whose method is not fully published, which is the opposite of the entry above and a useful contrast.

entries.name: Kaiko Market Data
entries.why: Institutional pricing sold under contract, listed as pass-through only.

entries.name: Binance Public Market Data
entries.why: Historical trade archives published as downloadable files, which is a large free dataset with restrictive terms.

entries.name: Bybit Public API
entries.why: Another venue for the same pairs, which is how a price disagreement becomes visible.

entries.name: OKX Public API
entries.why: A third venue, enough to show that "the price" is a choice rather than a fact.

entries.name: Bitstamp Public API
entries.why: One of the longest continuous price histories in the domain.

entries.name: Gemini Public API
entries.why: Publishes an auction price used as a settlement reference, which is an anchor with a stated rule.

entries.name: CME CF Cryptocurrency Reference Rates
entries.why: A regulated benchmark with a published methodology, which is the settleable anchor H1 requires before any accuracy claim.

entries.name: Chainlink Price Feeds
entries.why: On-chain aggregation of off-chain sources, which is a provenance design worth studying and arguing with.

entries.name: Pyth Network Price Feeds
entries.why: Publishes per-publisher contributions and a confidence interval, which is disagreement reported rather than hidden.

entries.name: Solana Public RPC
entries.why: High block rate, which makes staleness measurable in seconds rather than minutes.

entries.name: Cosmos SDK REST Endpoints
entries.why: A shared interface across many chains, so one adapter covers an ecosystem.

entries.name: Polkadot API Sidecar

entries.name: Bitquery GraphQL API
entries.why: Cross-chain queries sold per unit, another metered pass-through.

entries.why: A free research tier of a commercial product, which is a use-class split inside one publisher.

entries.name: Glassnode API
entries.why: Derived on-chain metrics whose definitions change without notice, which is an interpretation layer rather than a source.

entries.name: L2BEAT Data
entries.why: Publishes its assumptions alongside its numbers, which is the standard the rest of this file falls short of.

entries.name: Ethereum Beacon Chain API
entries.why: A standardised consensus-layer interface, so several client implementations can be compared answering the same question.

groups.description: Cultural heritage collections, media metadata, and sports results. The heritage half is slow, open, and heavily attributed, which exercises the attribution string in license_chain more than any other group. The sports half is the opposite: seconds matter, corrections are common during a game, and the settled result at the end is a genuine anchor. Phase 4 names graded sports feeds as a vertical, so these entries are targets rather than hypotheses.

entries.name: The Movie Database
entries.why: Community-edited film metadata with a daily export, so edits are diffable in bulk.

entries.name: Discogs
entries.why: Release metadata that overlaps MusicBrainz, so two community catalogs can be compared.

entries.name: ListenBrainz
entries.why: Listening statistics under CC0, joined to MusicBrainz identifiers we already plan to carry.

entries.name: Spotify Web API
entries.why: Catalog metadata behind per-user OAuth, which only works as pass-through. Terms almost certainly forbid the caching a router does, so read them before promising anything.

entries.name: Europeana
entries.why: An aggregator over thousands of institutions with per-item rights statements, which is a licence chain with a different licence on every row.

entries.name: Digital Public Library of America
entries.why: The US counterpart to Europeana, with the same per-item rights problem.

entries.name: Smithsonian Open Access
entries.why: CC0 collection records with stable identifiers, the simplest licence case in the group.

entries.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art Collection API
entries.why: No key, no quota, small payloads, which makes it a good first end-to-end console demo.

entries.name: Rijksmuseum API
entries.why: A national collection with strict attribution wording that must be reproduced verbatim.

entries.name: Harvard Art Museums API
entries.why: Records carry a lastupdate field, so freshness can be measured without guessing.

entries.name: Chronicling America
entries.why: OCR text of historical newspapers, which is bulk untrusted_text with no live risk.

entries.name: Library of Congress JSON API
entries.why: One API over many collections whose schemas differ, a real schema-stability workout.

entries.name: HathiTrust Bibliographic API
entries.why: Holdings and rights per volume, where the rights field is the point rather than a footnote.

entries.name: Directory of Open Access Journals
entries.why: Journal licensing metadata, which is the reference table a licence chain needs anyway.

entries.name: Project Gutenberg
entries.why: A catalog that is public domain in content but trademark-restricted in distribution, which is a licence nuance the schema should be able to express.

entries.name: Wikimedia Pageviews and REST API
entries.why: Hourly counts that are restated after bot filtering, a clean revision-behaviour example.

entries.name: New York Times Developer APIs
entries.why: Archive and books metadata under terms that will almost certainly block commercial use, which makes it a concrete test of the two-endpoint split in ADR-0008.

entries.name: MLB Stats API
entries.why: Live play-by-play that is corrected during and after a game, then settled officially. That settled result is a real anchor, which accuracy claims need under rule H1.

entries.name: NHL Web API
entries.why: A second league on the same pattern, unofficial docs only, so stability is the question.

entries.name: football-data.org
entries.why: A derivative results feed with a free tier, so its lag behind the league is measurable.

groups.description: Vulnerability catalogues, threat intelligence, and internet measurement. This group is the one where an agent is most likely to act on a tool result immediately, which makes two of our rules load-bearing at once: advisory text is attacker-controllable and belongs in untrusted_text (H5), and a vulnerability record that has been superseded is worse than no record at all. Candidates only, terms unread.

entries.name: NVD CVE API 2.0
entries.why: The versioned successor interface to the NVD entry already registered, with a strict rate limit that the envelope must report.

entries.name: CVE Services API (MITRE)
entries.why: Records appear here before NVD enriches them, which is a measurable lead-lag between two official publishers of the same identifier.

entries.name: CISA Vulnrichment
entries.why: Adds fields NVD has struggled to keep up with, which is a derivative created by a backlog.

entries.name: ENISA EU Vulnerability Database
entries.why: A second regional authority on the same vulnerabilities, so disagreement becomes visible.

entries.name: VulnCheck KEV
entries.why: A commercial superset of the CISA KEV entry already registered, which is a compare case with a paid counterparty.

entries.name: Exploit Database
entries.why: Proof-of-concept availability is a risk signal the official records do not carry.

entries.name: Metasploit Module Metadata
entries.why: Module release dates anchor claims about when exploitation became easy.

entries.name: CISA Cybersecurity Advisories
entries.why: Advisory text is narrative and attacker-referenced, a clear untrusted_text case.

entries.name: NCSC UK Advisories
entries.why: A second national authority whose timing can be compared with CISA's.

entries.name: BSI CERT-Bund Advisories
entries.why: German advisories that often cover products the anglophone feeds miss.

entries.name: JVN Japan Vulnerability Notes
entries.why: Publishes its own identifiers alongside CVE, which is an identifier mapping problem.

entries.name: CNNVD
entries.why: Known to publish and withhold on a different schedule from NVD, which is exactly the kind of difference a compare tool should surface rather than resolve.

entries.name: GitHub Security Advisories GraphQL
entries.why: The queryable interface behind the advisory entry already registered.

entries.name: GitLab Advisory Database
entries.why: An openly licensed advisory set built from different curation, so ranges often differ from GitHub's.

entries.name: OSV Vulnerability Feeds
entries.why: Per-ecosystem zip feeds beside the OSV API already registered, which is a bulk versus query trade-off.

entries.name: PyPA Advisory Database
entries.why: Ecosystem-specific curation that upstream aggregators consume, a clean lineage leaf.

entries.name: RustSec Advisory Database
entries.why: Community-maintained with a git history, so every change is already attributable.

entries.name: Ruby Advisory Database
entries.why: Another ecosystem leaf, useful for measuring how quickly aggregators pick up changes.

entries.name: Go Vulnerability Database
entries.why: Curated with explicit symbol-level detail, which is finer than any aggregator carries.

entries.name: Sonatype OSS Index
entries.why: A commercial index over the same ecosystems, which puts a price on the free feeds above.

entries.name: AbuseIPDB
entries.why: Crowd-reported rather than verified, which the envelope must not present as authoritative.

entries.name: AlienVault OTX
entries.why: Community pulses of wildly varying quality, a completeness and reliability contrast.

entries.name: URLhaus
entries.why: Frequently updated indicator feed released without restriction.

entries.name: PhishTank
entries.why: Entries expire and are re-verified, which is a lifecycle most indicator feeds lack.

entries.name: OpenPhish Community Feed
entries.why: The free tier is a deliberately delayed subset, which is a freshness difference sold as a product.

entries.name: Spamhaus DROP Lists
entries.why: Widely deployed lists whose terms restrict commercial redistribution, alongside the DBL entry already held.

entries.name: FireHOL IP Lists
entries.why: Aggregates dozens of lists with per-source attribution preserved in git, which is lineage done by hand.

entries.name: MITRE ATT&CK STIX Data
entries.why: Versioned releases that tooling pins to, so the version is part of any correct answer.

entries.name: MITRE CWE Catalog
entries.why: A classification other feeds encode against, revised on its own schedule.

entries.name: FIRST CVSS Specification Data
entries.why: Scores computed under different CVSS versions are not comparable, which is a method version problem the scorecard has too.

entries.name: Shadowserver Public Reports
entries.why: Scan-derived exposure data given to network owners, with strict conditions on reuse.

entries.name: SANS Internet Storm Center API
entries.why: Port activity aggregates that make scanning trends visible without running sensors.

entries.name: Cloudflare Radar API
entries.why: The keyed API beside the Radar entry already registered, with different terms from the public pages.

entries.name: RIPE Routing Information Service
entries.why: BGP updates in near real time, and an archive going back two decades.

entries.name: bgp.tools Data
entries.why: A community service with usage conditions, useful as a cross-check on the academic feeds.

entries.name: Internet Routing Registry Data
entries.why: Registries that disagree with observed routing, which is disagreement with operational consequences.

entries.name: RPKI Repository Data
entries.why: Cryptographically signed route origin authorisations, which is verifiable provenance in production somewhere other than here.

entries.name: Internet Society Pulse
entries.why: Country-level adoption metrics assembled from several measurement projects, a documented derivative.

entries.name: IODA Internet Outage Detection
entries.why: Outage signals from three independent methods published side by side, which is compare built into the source.

groups.description: Satellite and remote sensing archives, and the derived products built on them. Two properties make this group different from the rest of the registry. Products are reprocessed in numbered collections, so the same observation legitimately has several values and the collection is part of the answer; and volumes are large enough that fetching without caching is a cost decision rather than a performance one. Candidates only, terms unread.

entries.name: USGS EarthExplorer
entries.why: Landsat access requires an account even though the data is public domain, which separates licence from access control.

entries.name: Landsat Collection 2
entries.why: Collection 2 restated every Landsat scene ever taken, which is the largest reprocessing event any archive has published.

entries.name: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem
entries.why: Sentinel data with a documented open licence and a quota model that the envelope would have to report.

entries.name: Sentinel Hub
entries.why: A commercial front end over open data, which is the clearest possible example of a derivative charging for delivery rather than content.

entries.name: NASA Common Metadata Repository
entries.why: The catalogue behind NASA Earthdata, with collection versions exposed directly.

entries.name: NASA AppEEARS
entries.why: Produces subsets on request, so the response is computed rather than stored, which is a reproducibility question.

entries.name: NASA Worldview GIBS
entries.why: Tiled imagery with near-realtime layers, useful for demonstrating freshness visually.

entries.name: NASA POWER
entries.why: Solar and meteorological parameters derived from satellites, widely used in agriculture models.

entries.name: MODIS Land Products (LP DAAC)
entries.why: Long record with several collection versions still in active use at once.

entries.name: VIIRS Land Products
entries.why: The successor instrument, so continuity between the two is a real reconciliation problem.

entries.name: GOES-R ABI Imagery
entries.why: New imagery every few minutes on public cloud storage, the fastest large feed available free.

entries.name: Himawari Realtime Imagery
entries.why: Covers the Pacific basin the American satellites miss, which is a coverage gap in the literal sense.

entries.name: EUMETSAT Data Store
entries.why: European geostationary and polar products under a stated licence.

entries.name: ESA Earth Online
entries.why: Heritage missions whose archives are reprocessed decades after acquisition.

entries.name: JAXA G-Portal
entries.why: Japanese mission archive with terms that need reading before any redistribution.

entries.name: ISRO Bhuvan
entries.why: Indian imagery and derived layers, largely absent from western catalogues.

entries.name: Planet Labs API
entries.why: Commercial high-cadence imagery, only ever routable with the customer's own contract.

entries.name: Maxar Content APIs
entries.why: The other major commercial provider, recorded for the same reason.

entries.name: Umbra Open Data Program
entries.why: Commercially collected SAR released openly, which is a useful counterexample to the assumption that commercial means closed.

entries.name: Capella Space Open Data
entries.why: A second open SAR sample set, enough to compare two providers on one scene.

entries.name: ASF SAR Data Search
entries.why: The archive most InSAR research runs against, with per-mission terms.

entries.name: OpenTopography
entries.why: Elevation datasets with per-dataset citation requirements, which is attribution done strictly.

entries.name: Copernicus Digital Elevation Model
entries.why: A global elevation baseline that many derived products silently depend on.

entries.name: SRTM Elevation Data
entries.why: Twenty years old, still widely used, and quietly superseded, which is the definition of a staleness problem.

entries.name: ESA WorldCover
entries.why: Annual land cover with versions that disagree about the same pixel, a compare case.

entries.name: Esri Sentinel-2 Land Cover
entries.why: A second global land cover product built from the same inputs by a different method.

entries.name: Dynamic World Land Cover
entries.why: Near-realtime rather than annual, which makes the three-way comparison a genuine freshness versus stability trade-off.

entries.name: Global Forest Watch API
entries.why: Deforestation alerts with named methods and versions, and a policy audience that needs the version stated.

entries.name: GLAD Forest Loss Alerts
entries.why: The upstream alert layer behind several dashboards that never cite it.

entries.name: RADD Radar Deforestation Alerts

entries.name: MapBiomas
entries.why: Reprocesses its entire time series with each collection, so historical values change.

entries.name: Sentinel-5P TROPOMI Products
entries.why: Trace gas measurements with near-realtime and offline versions of the same orbit.

entries.name: GHGSat Public Data
entries.why: Methane plume detections that regulators and companies dispute, so provenance matters more than usual.

entries.name: Carbon Mapper Data Portal
entries.why: Publishes emission plume observations openly, complementing the commercial detections.

entries.name: NASA FIRMS Archive
entries.why: The archived counterpart to the FIRMS realtime entry already registered, with different quality flags.

entries.name: WorldPop API
entries.why: Modelled population grids that many humanitarian analyses treat as observed data.

entries.name: GHSL Global Human Settlement Layer
entries.why: A competing population grid with a different method, which is a compare case with real policy consequences.

entries.name: VIIRS Nighttime Lights
entries.why: Used as an economic proxy where official statistics are weak, which ties this file to the statistics ones.

entries.name: Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC
entries.why: A STAC catalogue over dozens of public collections, which is one adapter for many sources and a lineage layer we would have to disclose.

groups.description: Election authorities, parliamentary records, and legislative data. Election night is the single hardest freshness problem in public data: results are provisional for hours, corrected for weeks, certified once, and republished by dozens of derivatives that rarely say which vintage they hold. Parliamentary records are the opposite, slow and append-only, which makes the pair useful together. Candidates only, terms unread.

entries.name: AP Elections API
entries.why: The de facto US results primary, commercially licensed, so pass-through only.

entries.name: US Election Assistance Commission Data
entries.why: The settled biennial survey that election-night feeds can be graded against.

entries.name: MIT Election Data and Science Lab
entries.why: Cleaned historical results with documented version numbers, which is an anchor with a method.

entries.name: OpenElections
entries.why: Volunteer-compiled county results whose completeness varies by state, which is honest and measurable.

entries.name: California Secretary of State Election Results
entries.why: Counts continue changing for weeks after election night, the clearest late-revision case in US politics.

entries.name: Texas Secretary of State Election Results
entries.why: A second large state with a different certification timetable.

entries.name: Florida Division of Elections
entries.why: Publishes campaign finance alongside results, which links two demand areas.

entries.name: New York State Board of Elections
entries.why: Certification is slow enough that provisional and final differ materially.

entries.name: Elections Canada Results
entries.why: Publishes preliminary and validated counts as separate products, which is revision made explicit.

entries.name: UK Electoral Commission Data
entries.why: Donations and spending returns filed on a statutory clock, which makes lateness itself a datum.

entries.name: Democracy Club
entries.why: Community-maintained candidate and polling place data, openly licensed.

entries.name: Bundeswahlleiterin Election Results (Germany)
entries.why: Publishes constituency-level results with a formal correction procedure.

entries.name: Ministere de l'Interieur Election Results (France)

entries.name: Ministerio del Interior Election Results (Spain)
entries.why: Live counts during the night and a definitive file later, another two-vintage source.

entries.name: TSE Election Results (Brazil)

entries.name: INE Mexico Election Results

entries.name: Election Commission of India Results
entries.why: The largest election in the world, with a counting-day feed that many derivatives scrape.

entries.name: Australian Electoral Commission Tally Room

entries.name: New Zealand Electoral Commission Results

entries.name: International IDEA Voter Turnout Database

entries.name: ParlGov Database

entries.name: EveryPolitician Archive

entries.name: Wikidata Politician Records

entries.name: European Parliament Open Data Portal
entries.why: Roll-call votes and documents with persistent identifiers and an open licence.

entries.name: Council of the EU Voting Records
entries.why: The other half of the EU legislative record, published separately.

entries.name: Bundestag DIP API (Germany)
entries.why: A real API over parliamentary process documents, which is rare outside the anglophone world.

entries.name: Assemblee nationale Open Data (France)

entries.name: Congreso de los Diputados Open Data

entries.name: Tweede Kamer Open Data (Netherlands)

Emissions inventories sit at the other end: annual, heavily restated, and mostly derivative.

That makes revision behaviour and correction latency measurable without any external anchor, which is why the group is worth this much of the registry. Candidates only.

groups.description: Disasters, hazards, and environmental monitoring. An alert feed is the one place where every dimension we measure has an obvious cost attached: late is dangerous, wrong is worse, and a silent revision after the fact is how people stop trusting a source. Several entries here duplicate each other deliberately, because two agencies reporting the same earthquake with different magnitudes is the clearest possible demonstration of what compare is for.

entries.why: A multi-hazard alert layer over other agencies, which makes it derivative by design.

entries.name: EM-DAT International Disaster Database
entries.why: Disaster losses restated for years after the event, which is correction latency at the scale of decades rather than minutes.

entries.name: ReliefWeb
entries.why: Situation reports as documents, so the payload is untrusted_text almost end to end.

entries.name: USGS Volcano Hazards Program
entries.why: Alert level changes with an explicit issue time, which is a state machine with timestamps.

entries.name: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program
entries.why: The global catalog USGS reports flow into weekly, a lineage pair with a known lag.

entries.name: NASA FIRMS Active Fire Data
entries.why: Near-real-time detections replaced by standard-quality ones days later, so the same fire appears twice with different values. A revision-behaviour example that needs no explanation.

entries.name: European Forest Fire Information System
entries.why: A regional derivative of FIRMS, which lets a lineage claim be checked against a peer.

entries.name: InciWeb
entries.why: Incident narratives updated irregularly by hand, so freshness varies wildly by incident.

entries.name: NIFC Open Data
entries.why: Perimeters and situation reports with edit timestamps, the structured half of InciWeb.

entries.name: NOAA National Hurricane Center
entries.why: Advisories every three hours on a fixed clock, with forecast tracks that can be scored against the track that actually happened. A rare anchored accuracy case.

entries.name: IBTrACS Tropical Cyclone Best Track
entries.why: The settled reanalysis of storms, which is the anchor NHC forecasts are scored against.

entries.name: US Drought Monitor
entries.why: A weekly expert judgement over several inputs, so the method is human and documented.

entries.name: NSIDC Sea Ice Index
entries.why: Daily near-real-time values later replaced by a final product, clearly labelled as such.

entries.name: Copernicus Emergency Management Service
entries.why: Activation-based mapping, so coverage is zero until an event, which segments completeness.

entries.name: European Environment Agency Air Quality
entries.why: Up-to-date and validated streams of the same stations, published as separate products.

entries.name: EPA Air Quality System
entries.why: The certified archive behind AirNow, which is already in the registry as the fast feed. Together they are a freshness and accuracy trade-off with both ends in our hands.

entries.name: EPA Toxics Release Inventory

entries.name: NOAA Tsunami Warning Centers
entries.why: Messages issued and then cancelled, where the cancellation matters as much as the alert.

entries.name: EMSC Seismic Portal
entries.why: Reports the same earthquakes as usgs-earthquake, our first merged source, with a different magnitude and a different lag. That disagreement is the demo the compare tool exists for, against a source whose catalog entry is already written.

entries.name: GFZ GEOFON
entries.why: A third seismic network, which turns a two-way disagreement into a majority question.

groups.description: Central banks, international statistical agencies, market data, and crypto. Financial data is where redistribution terms bite hardest: several widely used endpoints are free to call and still forbid republication, which is exactly the distinction the licence chain exists to carry. Nothing here is promoted without reading the terms in full.

entries.name: ECB euro foreign exchange reference rates
entries.why: Published once daily at a fixed time, so it is a cheap and exact accuracy anchor for FX.

entries.name: Frankfurter
entries.why: Open-source republisher of ECB rates, so the lineage pair needs no licence negotiation.

entries.name: Bank of England statistics
entries.why: A second central bank, for release-schedule comparison outside the United States.

entries.name: IMF Data
entries.why: International macro series, heavily revised between vintages.

entries.name: World Bank Open Data
entries.why: Aggregates national statistics agencies, a broad lineage graph in one source.

entries.name: OECD Data Explorer
entries.why: Another derivative of national agencies, useful for republish-lag comparison.

entries.name: Eurostat
entries.why: European official statistics with a published release calendar.

entries.name: Statistics Canada

entries.name: UK Office for National Statistics

entries.name: Australian Bureau of Statistics
entries.why: Southern hemisphere coverage and a different release calendar shape.

entries.name: US Treasury yield curve rates
entries.why: Daily at a known time, and republished by many vendors, so lineage is easy to prove.

entries.name: CFTC Commitments of Traders
entries.why: Weekly on a fixed schedule with occasional republished corrections.

entries.name: SEC Financial Statement Data Sets
entries.why: Quarterly bulk companion to EDGAR, where restatements become visible in aggregate.

entries.name: CoinGecko

entries.name: Polygon.io

entries.name: Finnhub

entries.name: Nasdaq Data Link
entries.why: Mixed free and licensed datasets under one key, so per-dataset terms must be chained.

groups.description: Securities regulators, prudential supervisors, and the disclosure systems they run. Filings are the ideal shape for a provenance envelope: each one has an accession identifier, a filing timestamp, an amendment chain, and a legal consequence for being wrong. The interesting scoring question here is not freshness but correction latency, since an amended filing supersedes an original that many downstreams never revisit. Candidates only, terms unread.

entries.name: SEC EDGAR Full-Text Search API
entries.why: A different interface over the EDGAR corpus already registered, with its own rate limits.

entries.name: SEC Form 13F Holdings
entries.why: Quarterly with a 45-day lag and frequent amendments, which makes the vintage essential.

entries.name: SEC Form D Offerings
entries.why: Private placement notices filed continuously, a genuine change feed.

entries.name: SEC Investment Adviser Public Disclosure
entries.why: Adviser records amended annually, with disciplinary history appended rather than replaced.

entries.name: FINRA OTC Transparency Data
entries.why: Weekly volume data with a delayed publication rule set by regulation, not by the publisher.

entries.name: FINRA BrokerCheck
entries.why: Individual records that change when disclosures are added, with obvious privacy handling questions.

entries.name: MSRB EMMA Municipal Disclosure
entries.why: Municipal bond disclosures filed irregularly, where absence is itself informative.

entries.name: CFTC Swaps Reports
entries.why: Weekly aggregates revised on republication, alongside the COT entry already registered.

entries.name: NFA BASIC Registration Records

entries.name: Federal Reserve National Information Center
entries.why: Bank ownership hierarchies, which is the structural reference data behind most bank analysis.

entries.name: FDIC BankFind API
entries.why: Institution and financial data with a documented API, and failures published the day they happen.

entries.name: NCUA Credit Union Data
entries.why: The credit union counterpart to the FDIC data, filed quarterly.

entries.name: FFIEC Call Reports
entries.why: Amended filings are common and the original stays retrievable, which is a clean revision pair.

entries.name: FFIEC HMDA Mortgage Data
entries.why: Annual releases with a separate corrected version published months later.

entries.name: FHFA House Price Index
entries.why: Revised each quarter for several quarters back, a textbook revision profile.

entries.name: TreasuryDirect Auction Results

entries.name: Treasury International Capital System
entries.why: Monthly with a two-month lag and large back revisions.

entries.name: ESMA Registers and Data
entries.why: Reference registers that European market data joins against, published openly.

entries.name: ESMA FIRDS Instrument Reference

entries.name: European Banking Authority Risk Dashboard
entries.why: Quarterly supervisory aggregates with restated history.

entries.name: EIOPA Insurance Statistics
entries.why: Insurance data is thin everywhere, so this is coverage rather than duplication.

entries.name: FCA Financial Services Register
entries.why: Authorisation status changes daily, which is the permission a compliance agent needs checked live.

entries.name: Bank of England Statistical Database
entries.why: A distinct product from the rate feed already registered, with long revised series.

entries.name: PRA Regulatory Data
entries.why: Bank capital data published on a supervisory rather than a market clock.

entries.name: BaFin Databases (Germany)
entries.why: Short-selling and voting-rights notifications, which are event feeds with legal deadlines.

entries.name: AMF France Decisions and Registers
entries.why: Sanction decisions and disclosure filings from one publisher.

entries.name: CONSOB Registers (Italy)
entries.why: Completes the large EU supervisors for cross-border comparison.

entries.name: CNMV Registers (Spain)
entries.why: Publishes filings in a structured format with stable identifiers.

entries.name: SEDAR+ (Canada)
entries.why: The Canadian filing system, with terms that are stricter than EDGAR's and need reading.

entries.name: ASIC Registers (Australia)
entries.why: Company and licensee data behind a paid search, which is a pass-through candidate.

entries.name: EDINET (Japan FSA)
entries.why: Japanese filings in XBRL with a documented API, structurally similar to EDGAR.

entries.name: DART (Korea FSS)
entries.why: Korean disclosure filings with an open API and English metadata.

entries.name: HKEX News Disclosure
entries.why: Announcements published continuously during trading hours, where minutes matter.

entries.name: SGX Company Announcements
entries.why: Exchange-operated disclosure with commercial terms on the same public facts.

entries.name: SEBI Filings and Orders (India)
entries.why: Regulatory orders published as PDFs, which is parsing cost in a domain that needs accuracy.

entries.name: CVM Open Data (Brazil)
entries.why: Fund and issuer data published as open bulk files, which is unusually generous for a securities regulator.

entries.name: BIS Locational and Consolidated Banking Statistics
entries.why: Quarterly with systematic back revisions, and built from national submissions with differing completeness.

entries.name: Financial Stability Board Global Monitoring Report Data
entries.why: An annual derivative of the national supervisors above, with a published methodology.

entries.name: IMF Financial Soundness Indicators
entries.why: Country-submitted indicators with metadata describing each country's deviations, which is completeness documented by the publisher.

entries.name: World Bank Global Findex
entries.why: Survey waves years apart, which makes the freshness dimension a question of what the series is for rather than how old it is.

groups.description: Geography, mapping, aviation, marine, transit, and earth observation. This group has the tightest freshness requirements in the catalog, measured in seconds rather than hours, and it contains several sources whose terms restrict commercial use or redistribution, so the licence reading here matters more than anywhere else.

entries.name: OpenStreetMap Overpass API
entries.notes: ODbL share-alike plus a published usage policy. Needs careful reading before promotion.
entries.why: The clearest share-alike case we would route to, which forces licence chaining to work.

entries.name: Nominatim geocoding
entries.why: Geocoding, though the public instance has a strict usage policy we must respect.

entries.name: GeoNames
entries.why: Place name resolution across countries.

entries.name: Natural Earth
entries.why: Public domain basemap geometry with no attribution burden at all.

entries.name: Census TIGER/Line
entries.why: US boundary geometry, the join layer for every segment breakdown we publish.

entries.name: Aviation Weather Center METAR and TAF
entries.why: TAF forecasts graded by later METAR observations. A second anchor, same shape as NWS.

entries.name: FAA National Airspace System Status
entries.why: Ground stops and delays, where a minute of staleness changes the answer.

entries.name: FAA Aircraft Registry
entries.why: Slow-moving registry, a good schema stability baseline over years.

entries.name: OpenSky Network
entries.notes: Believed non-commercial for the free tier. Under ADR-0008 that makes it a free-endpoint source only. Confirm before promotion; this is exactly the case use classes exist for.
entries.why: Live aircraft positions, and the second non-commercial source after Open-Meteo.

entries.name: NOAA CO-OPS Tides and Currents
entries.why: Publishes predictions and verified water levels separately. A mechanical accuracy anchor.

entries.name: NOAA National Data Buoy Center
entries.why: Sensor dropouts are common and visible, which makes completeness by segment real.

entries.name: MTA GTFS-realtime
entries.why: Sub-minute freshness, which stresses the p95 lag measurement harder than anything else.

entries.name: BART GTFS-realtime
entries.why: Second transit feed, for cross-agency comparison of the same data shape.

entries.name: WMATA GTFS and realtime
entries.why: Transit coverage in a third metro area.

entries.name: Transitland
entries.why: Aggregator of agency feeds, so it is a lineage pair with each agency source.

entries.name: Bureau of Transportation Statistics
entries.why: On-time performance, published monthly on a fixed schedule.

entries.name: Copernicus Data Space
entries.why: Sentinel imagery, free and open, with a large object size worth cost modelling.

entries.name: NASA Earthdata
entries.why: Earth science across many instruments, with reprocessing as a revision event.

entries.name: NASA Open APIs
entries.why: Near-earth objects and space weather, with a free demo key for quick testing.

entries.name: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center
entries.why: Forecasts and observations in the same feed family, so accuracy is anchorable.

groups.description: United States federal statistical, regulatory, and fiscal feeds. Most works of the US federal government are public domain under 17 U.S.C. 105, but that is a rule about authorship and not a substitute for reading a given agency's own terms, so every entry here still starts at license_status unverified. Five entries are promoted because their terms were read and cited during Phase 0.

entries.name: National Weather Service API
entries.why: Primary US weather, and the accuracy anchor where observations grade earlier forecasts.

entries.name: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program
entries.why: Magnitudes are revised after publication, which is the clearest revision behaviour we have.

entries.name: Bureau of Labor Statistics Public Data API
entries.why: Scheduled releases, so freshness lag can be measured against a published calendar.

entries.name: Federal Reserve Economic Data
entries.notes: Listed as FRED's own terms of use, not public domain. Individual series carry the terms of their originating source, which is why per-series origin notes are required.
entries.why: Republishes BLS, so republish lag is measurable and validates lineage inference.

entries.name: Open-Meteo
entries.notes: Free tier is non-commercial. Under ADR-0008 it routes only for callers who declared noncommercial, or for commercial callers who bring their own paid plan credentials.
entries.why: Derivative of NWS and others, so it demonstrates lineage lag and field disagreement.

entries.name: Bureau of Economic Analysis
entries.why: GDP advance, second, and third estimates are the cleanest revision story in public data.

entries.name: US Census American Community Survey
entries.why: Vintage-based revision and completeness that genuinely varies by geographic segment.

entries.name: US Treasury Fiscal Data
entries.why: Daily scheduled releases with exact publication times and no key required.

entries.name: Energy Information Administration
entries.why: Weekly petroleum and electricity series with routine revisions.

entries.name: SEC EDGAR
entries.notes: Requires a declared User-Agent and respects a published request rate limit.
entries.why: Restatements are revisions with legal weight, and filings carry exact acceptance times.

entries.name: Federal Register API
entries.why: Daily regulatory publication with a stable schema over a long horizon.

entries.name: Regulations.gov
entries.why: Rulemaking dockets and public comments for regulatory agents.

entries.name: USAspending
entries.why: Federal award data that is corrected heavily after first publication.

entries.name: Data.gov catalog
entries.why: A catalog of catalogs, and the fastest route to finding further candidates.

entries.name: Federal Election Commission
entries.why: Filing amendments are frequent and explicit, so revision behaviour is easy to score.

entries.name: Congress.gov API
entries.why: Bill status with defined stages, useful for correction latency.

entries.name: CPSC Recalls
entries.why: Consumer product recalls, part of the regulatory wedge alongside openFDA.

entries.name: NHTSA Recalls and Complaints
entries.why: Vehicle recalls and complaints, with duplicate reporting worth detecting.

entries.name: IRS Statistics of Income
entries.why: Slow-moving tax statistics, a good completeness-by-segment case.

entries.name: USPS ZIP Code lookup
entries.why: Address normalisation, a common preprocessing step before any geographic query.

groups.description: Public health agencies, medicines regulators, and disease surveillance systems. This group has the highest cost of a stale or wrong answer in the whole registry, and the worst revision discipline: case counts are backfilled for weeks, definitions change mid-series, and agencies routinely republish each other without saying so. It is the strongest argument for the envelope. Candidates only, terms unread.

entries.name: ECDC Surveillance Atlas
entries.why: European case data with explicit reporting-week semantics, so backfill is visible instead of implied.

entries.name: ERVISS Respiratory Virus Surveillance
entries.why: Weekly multi-country reporting where late countries are flagged rather than dropped.

entries.name: CDC FluView
entries.why: Every week revises the previous several weeks, which is the clearest revision pattern in US public health data.

entries.name: CDC National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance
entries.why: State-reported counts with jurisdiction-level completeness differences.

entries.name: CDC NCHS Provisional Mortality
entries.why: Provisional and final versions of the same count are both published, which is revision behaviour by design.

entries.name: CDC BRFSS Survey Data
entries.why: Survey weights change between releases, which is a schema stability issue disguised as a data one.

entries.name: CDC NHANES
entries.why: Released in fixed cycles with documented file versions, which makes as_of replay exact.

entries.name: CMS Open Payments
entries.why: Annual publication with a dispute window, so records legitimately change after release.

entries.name: CMS Provider Data Catalog
entries.why: Quality ratings that downstream sites republish without the measurement period attached.

entries.name: CMS Hospital Price Transparency Files
entries.why: Thousands of hospitals publishing to a mandated schema with wildly varying compliance, which is a completeness measurement with real stakes.

entries.name: HRSA Data Warehouse
entries.why: Facility and shortage-area designations that change on an administrative clock.

entries.name: SAMHSA Behavioral Health Data
entries.why: Suppressed small cells throughout, which is the case H15 exists for.

entries.name: AHRQ HCUP Databases
entries.why: Requires a data use agreement, so it can only ever be routed with the customer's own access.

entries.name: FDA FAERS Quarterly Files
entries.why: The raw quarterly files behind the openFDA entry already registered, which is a lineage pair inside one agency.

entries.name: FDA Drug Shortages
entries.why: Status changes are discrete, dated, and consequential, which is a change feed somebody would actually pay for.

entries.name: FDA Enforcement Reports
entries.why: Classification of a recall can change after publication, a correction latency case.

entries.name: European Medicines Agency Medicine Data
entries.why: Authorisation decisions with effective dates, and the European counterpart to FDA records.

entries.name: EudraVigilance Public Data
entries.why: Adverse event reports that FAERS also partly covers, which is genuine cross-agency disagreement.

entries.name: MHRA Drug Safety Update
entries.why: A third regulator on the same molecules, completing a comparison set.

entries.name: PMDA (Japan) Review Reports
entries.why: Approvals published in Japanese first, which is a language and timing lag in one.

entries.name: Health Canada Drug Product Database
entries.why: Product records with a documented update cycle and an open licence.

entries.name: TGA Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods
entries.why: Another national register on the same products, which strengthens the comparison set.

entries.name: WHO FluNet
entries.why: Country-submitted laboratory data with visible reporting gaps.

entries.name: WHO Disease Outbreak News
entries.why: Narrative text that must stay in untrusted_text, which is a useful worked example of H5.

entries.name: WHO ICD API
entries.why: A versioned classification that other datasets encode against, so its version is part of their provenance whether they say so or not.

entries.name: WHO Immunization Data Portal
entries.why: Country estimates and country reports are published side by side and disagree, which is what compare is for.

entries.name: UNAIDS AIDSinfo
entries.why: Modelled estimates with published uncertainty bounds, which the envelope should carry rather than flatten.

entries.name: Global Fund Data Explorer
entries.why: Disbursement data that links health outcomes to financing, useful to the demand register.

entries.name: Gavi Country Data
entries.why: Another financing publisher on the same programmes, so figures can be reconciled.

entries.name: IHME Global Burden of Disease Results
entries.why: Widely cited modelled estimates under non-commercial terms, which is a clear free-versus- pro routing distinction.

entries.name: IHME COVID-19 Projections Archive
entries.why: An archive of forecasts that were later falsifiable, which is the rarest and most useful kind of accuracy anchor.

entries.name: NHS England Statistics
entries.why: Monthly waiting list data published on a fixed day, and revised the following month.

entries.name: UKHSA Syndromic Surveillance
entries.why: Daily indicators that lead the weekly official series, a lead-lag pair worth publishing.

entries.name: Robert Koch Institute Open Data
entries.why: Publishes a full daily archive on a public repository, which is a ready-made snapshot history.

entries.name: Sante publique France Open Data
entries.why: Published through the national portal with dataset-level update metadata.

entries.name: Istituto Superiore di Sanita Data
entries.why: Regional breakdowns whose definitions differ from the national total, a reconciliation case.

entries.name: NICD South Africa Surveillance
entries.why: The regional reference laboratory whose reports WHO republishes.

entries.name: Africa CDC Data Hub
entries.why: A continental aggregator with explicit member-state reporting status, which is completeness measured by the publisher itself.

entries.name: HealthMap
entries.why: Aggregates news reports into signals, which means its inputs are untrusted text by construction.

entries.name: ProMED-mail
entries.why: Expert-moderated outbreak reports, the earliest signal in many events and squarely free text.

entries.name: OpenPrescribing
entries.why: A derived analysis layer over NHS data with its own method version, which is the shape Kourob would take.

entries.name: RxNav and RxNorm API
entries.why: The interface layer over the RxNorm entry already registered, released monthly.

entries.name: UMLS Terminology Services
entries.why: Licence requires individual registration, which makes it pass-through only under H3.

entries.name: SNOMED CT Browser API

entries.name: LOINC
