groups.description: Routing, addressing, naming, measurement, and abuse data. Several of these are the closest public analogue to what Trooth does, in that they are measurement platforms that publish both a reading and the vantage point it was taken from. That makes them useful as prior art as well as as sources. It is also the group with the highest density of terms that forbid redistribution outright, which is worth learning early rather than late.

entries.name: RIPEstat
entries.why: Prefix, ASN, and whois views with a data_call_status field stating its own freshness.

entries.name: RIPE Atlas
entries.why: Measurements carry the probe that produced them, which is provenance done properly.

entries.name: University of Oregon Route Views
entries.why: Raw BGP archives on a fixed dump interval, so lateness is measurable to the minute.

entries.name: CAIDA BGPStream
entries.why: A derivative of Route Views and RIS, which is a lineage chain with three named hops.

entries.name: CAIDA AS Rank
entries.why: Inferred relationships, so the method version matters more than the observation date.

entries.name: PeeringDB
entries.why: Self-reported facility data, stale in exactly the way self-reported data always is.

entries.name: IPinfo
entries.why: IP geolocation where three vendors disagree constantly, which is a compare demo.

entries.name: MaxMind GeoLite2
entries.why: The second opinion IPinfo needs, on a weekly build cadence with a signed release.

entries.name: IANA RDAP Bootstrap
entries.why: The registry of registries for domain lookups, small and authoritative.

entries.name: ICANN Centralized Zone Data Service
entries.why: Zone files need a per-requester agreement per TLD, which is the pass-through model exactly.

entries.name: crt.sh Certificate Transparency
entries.why: A live append-only log with inclusion proofs, which is the Phase 2 design we plan to copy.

entries.name: Censys Search
entries.why: Host scan results with a stated scan time per record, which is freshness stated honestly.

entries.name: Shodan
entries.why: The other scanner, which makes scan staleness comparable rather than absolute.

entries.name: Cloudflare Radar
entries.why: Traffic and outage signals from one vantage point, which is the caveat worth carrying.

entries.name: OONI Measurements

entries.name: Measurement Lab
entries.why: Public performance tests, where the pipeline restates results after post-processing.

entries.name: abuse.ch URLhaus and ThreatFox
entries.why: Indicator feeds where an entry going stale has a direct operational cost.

entries.name: Spamhaus Domain Block List
entries.reason: Free use is limited to low-volume direct queries and explicitly excludes redistribution or commercial resale. A router in front of it is the disallowed case, so this is named here only so the question is not asked again.

entries.name: Tranco List

entries.name: Majestic Million
entries.why: One of Tranco's inputs, which turns that lineage claim into something checkable.

groups.description: Population, labour, migration, and education statistics. Almost everything here is a survey, which means published confidence intervals, suppressed cells in small geographies, and scheduled restatements. That makes the group the best available test of completeness by segment: a national total that looks fine while half the sub-geographies are blank.

entries.name: ILOSTAT
entries.why: Labour statistics for 180-odd countries, sourced from national offices with visible lag.

entries.name: UN World Population Prospects
entries.why: A biennial revision that restates history as well as projections, labelled by revision year.

entries.name: UNdata
entries.why: An aggregator over dozens of UN agencies, so every series here has a primary elsewhere.

entries.name: UNDP Human Development Reports
entries.why: A composite index whose inputs are all elsewhere in the registry, good for lineage demos.

entries.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics

entries.name: UNHCR Refugee Data Finder
entries.why: Population-of-concern figures revised mid-year as situations are reassessed.

entries.name: IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix
entries.why: Round-based field assessments, so the freshness question is which round, not which day.

entries.reason: Access requires a per-researcher agreement that forbids redistributing extracts. A router cannot honour a per-user agreement on the caller's behalf, so this stays out of the catalog unless the caller brings their own account under Phase 2 pass-through.
entries.why: The cleanest harmonised census microdata anywhere, and the clearest licence wall.

entries.name: US Census Population Estimates Program

entries.name: Current Population Survey

entries.name: Business Dynamics Statistics
entries.why: Firm entry and exit with disclosure-suppressed cells, a completeness case with a reason.

entries.name: County Business Patterns
entries.why: Employment by county and industry, where noise infusion changes values between vintages.

entries.name: USAJOBS
entries.why: Live postings that appear and vanish, so the archive is the only record of what existed.

entries.name: O*NET Web Services
entries.why: The occupation taxonomy other job data joins on, versioned explicitly by release.

entries.name: NCES IPEDS
entries.why: Institution-level reporting with provisional and revised releases of the same year.

entries.name: College Scorecard

entries.name: DOL OFLC Performance Data

entries.name: Social Security Administration Open Data
entries.why: Name frequencies and benefit statistics, annual and stable, a good schema-stability baseline.

entries.name: WorldPop
entries.why: Modelled gridded population, so the method version matters more than the timestamp.

entries.name: Human Mortality Database

groups.description: Court records, legislation, patents, and trademarks. Two things make this group distinctive. Documents are append-only by nature, which suits an archive, and several of the richest sources charge per page or per seat, which puts the licence question first rather than last. Nothing here is routable until the terms are read, and several entries exist to record a no.

entries.name: CourtListener and RECAP
entries.why: Federal dockets mirrored from PACER, with an explicit date_modified per docket entry.

entries.name: PACER
entries.reason: PACER charges per page retrieved. A router that fetches on a caller's behalf would be spending the customer's money per request, which needs pass-through credentials, a cost ceiling in the envelope, and terms review. None of that exists before Phase 2.
entries.why: The primary that CourtListener is derivative of, which is why the lineage matters.

entries.name: GovInfo
entries.why: Bills, opinions, and the CFR with authenticated PDFs, so hashes can be checked upstream.

entries.name: Caselaw Access Project
entries.why: Digitised state reporters back to 1658, a static corpus that tests as_of replay cheaply.

entries.name: EUR-Lex
entries.why: EU law in 24 languages, where completeness by language is a real segment gap.

entries.name: legislation.gov.uk
entries.why: Point-in-time versions of every statute, which is exactly the as_of model we sell.

groups.description: State-level open data portals in the United States. Most run on a handful of platforms, which is the reason to register them together: one declarative adapter per platform covers dozens of publishers, and the differences that remain are exactly the ones worth scoring. Several states have no central portal and appear here without a homepage until someone confirms one. All entries are candidates and none has had its terms read.

entries.name: Alabama Open Data Portal
entries.why: Socrata platform, so it shares an adapter with a dozen other states.

entries.name: Alaska Open Data Geoportal
entries.why: Alaska publishes mostly geospatial rather than tabular data, which tests whether the catalog shape assumes tables.

entries.name: Arizona Open Data
entries.why: State portal with water and land datasets no federal source carries at this resolution.

entries.name: Arkansas GIS Office Data
entries.why: Fills a gap where no general-purpose state portal exists.

entries.name: California Open Data Portal
entries.why: CKAN with per-dataset licence fields, and drought and water datasets that update daily.

entries.name: Colorado Information Marketplace
entries.why: Business registration filings update daily, which is a change-feed candidate.

entries.name: Connecticut Open Data
entries.why: Long-running Socrata instance with stable dataset identifiers.

entries.name: Delaware Open Data
entries.why: Small state, high corporate registration volume, which is a niche demand entries keep pointing at.

entries.name: Florida Geographic Data Library
entries.why: Florida has no single tabular portal, so coverage has to be assembled from agencies.

entries.name: Georgia GIS Clearinghouse
entries.why: Another state without a central tabular portal, worth recording so nobody looks twice.

entries.name: Hawaii Open Data
entries.why: Island-scale energy and tourism series with no federal equivalent.

entries.name: Idaho Open Data
entries.why: Water rights and rangeland data that only the state publishes.

entries.name: Illinois Data Portal
entries.why: State portal whose datasets Chicago's portal partly duplicates, a local lineage case.

entries.name: Indiana Management Performance Hub
entries.why: One of the few states that treats data quality as an explicit program, which is worth comparing against our own measurements.

entries.name: Iowa Open Data
entries.why: Agricultural and liquor sales datasets that update on a weekly clock.

entries.name: Kansas Data Access and Support Center
entries.why: Groundwater and aquifer series relevant to the drought feeds already registered.

entries.name: Kentucky Open Data
entries.why: Coal production and mine safety detail the federal series aggregate away.

entries.name: Louisiana Open Data
entries.why: Coastal loss and storm response data with a local publication clock.

entries.name: Maine GeoLibrary
entries.why: Fisheries and forestry layers not held federally at this resolution.

entries.name: Maryland Open Data
entries.why: Chesapeake water quality datasets updated on a stated schedule.

entries.name: Massachusetts Open Data
entries.why: Health and transport datasets are spread across agencies, which is itself a discovery problem worth solving.

entries.name: Michigan Open Data
entries.why: Great Lakes water and manufacturing employment series at state granularity.

entries.name: Minnesota Geospatial Commons
entries.why: Publishes explicit per-layer licence metadata, which is what H3 needs and most portals omit.

entries.name: Mississippi Automated Resource Information System
entries.why: The only state-level clearinghouse in a state with no general portal.

entries.name: Missouri Open Data
entries.why: State spending datasets refreshed monthly, which suits a change feed.

entries.name: Montana State Library Geographic Information
entries.why: Wildfire and land cover layers complementary to the federal fire feeds.

entries.name: Nebraska Open Data
entries.why: Irrigation and groundwater data used by the agricultural demand entries.

entries.name: Nevada Open Data
entries.why: Gaming revenue reports on a fixed monthly clock with no substitute publisher.

entries.name: New Hampshire GRANIT
entries.why: A university-hosted state clearinghouse, which raises a different licence question than a government portal.

entries.name: New Jersey Open Data Center
entries.why: Dense population, frequent environmental releases, and a Socrata adapter already shared.

entries.name: New Mexico Open Data
entries.why: Oil and gas permitting detail that the federal aggregates lag badly.

entries.name: New York State Open Data
entries.why: One of the largest Socrata instances, with datasets that revise silently, which is exactly what the diff job exists to catch.

entries.name: NC OneMap
entries.why: Statewide geospatial with documented update cycles per layer.

entries.name: North Dakota GIS Hub
entries.why: Bakken production data published faster by the state than by EIA.

entries.name: Ohio Open Data
entries.why: State portal with a documented dataset inventory that changes often.

entries.name: Oklahoma Open Data
entries.why: Induced seismicity records that pair directly with the USGS earthquake source already merged.

entries.name: Oregon Geospatial Data
entries.why: Forestry and wildfire layers with a faster clock than the national feeds.

entries.name: Pennsylvania Open Data
entries.why: Gas well production filings published quarterly with frequent back-corrections.

entries.name: Rhode Island Open Data
entries.why: Smallest state portal, useful as a minimum-volume case.

entries.name: South Carolina Open Data
entries.why: Coastal and port activity data with no faster upstream.

entries.name: South Dakota Open Data
entries.why: Agricultural and tribal-area statistics thin at the federal level.

entries.name: Tennessee Open Data
entries.why: Health and education datasets published by department rather than centrally.

entries.name: Texas Open Data Portal
entries.why: Large Socrata instance, and the state whose grid and oil data the energy feeds keep needing.

entries.name: Utah Open Data
entries.why: Water and air quality series relevant to the environmental feeds already listed.

entries.name: Vermont Open Geodata Portal
entries.why: Publishes update timestamps per layer, which makes freshness measurable without a scrape.

entries.name: Virginia Open Data Portal
entries.why: Aggregates agency datasets under one catalogue with mixed licences, which is a licence chain problem in miniature.

entries.name: Washington State Open Data
entries.why: Electric vehicle registration data that is widely republished without attribution, which makes it a good lineage demonstration.

entries.name: West Virginia GIS Technical Center
entries.why: Mining and terrain data held nowhere else at this detail.

entries.name: Wisconsin Open Data
entries.why: Dairy and groundwater series with a state-specific release calendar.

entries.name: Wyoming Open Data
entries.why: Coal and trona production reported by the state before federal republication.

entries.name: Open Data DC

entries.name: Puerto Rico Open Data
entries.why: Territory data that is routinely missing from national aggregates, which completeness scoring should surface rather than hide.

groups.description: Encyclopaedic and reference corpora, plus security advisory feeds. The reference sources are where schema drift and revision behaviour are most extreme, which makes them good stress tests. The security feeds are the clearest case of correction latency mattering to somebody: a CVE amended a week late is a week of wrong answers.

entries.name: Wikidata
entries.why: CC0, edited constantly, so it is the most extreme revision behaviour we could score.

entries.name: Wikipedia API
entries.why: Share-alike text and an enormous untrusted-text surface. Both worth handling properly.

entries.name: DBpedia
entries.why: Structured derivative of Wikipedia, so the lag is measurable against the primary.

entries.name: Open Library
entries.why: Bibliographic records, community edited, with steady completeness improvement.

entries.name: Internet Archive
entries.why: Wayback captures are a second opinion on what a source said at a past time.

entries.name: MusicBrainz
entries.why: Open music metadata with a strict rate limit and a clear attribution policy.

entries.name: Open Food Facts
entries.why: Crowd-sourced product data where completeness varies enormously by country segment.

entries.name: Open Brewery DB
entries.why: Small, stable, and free. A useful low-stakes fixture for adapter tests.

entries.name: Nager.Date public holidays
entries.why: Holiday calendars, which every release-schedule calculation eventually needs.

entries.name: REST Countries
entries.why: Country reference data, the join key for international sources.

entries.name: IANA root zone and TLD registry
entries.why: Rarely changes, so it is an excellent schema-stability control case.

entries.name: Public Suffix List
entries.why: Underpins any domain-level grouping we do, and changes in small reviewable diffs.

entries.name: Unicode CLDR
entries.why: Locale data on a fixed twice-yearly release schedule.

entries.name: NVD CVE API
entries.why: Severity scores are revised after publication, and lateness has a real security cost.

entries.name: CVE Program records
entries.why: The primary that NVD enriches, so the pair proves lineage in a domain people care about.

entries.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities
entries.why: Small, authoritative, appended on a schedule. A clean freshness case.

entries.name: GitHub Advisory Database
entries.why: Package-level advisories, another derivative of CVE with its own curation lag.

entries.name: OSV.dev
entries.why: Open vulnerability format aggregating several databases, so disagreement is visible.

entries.name: EPSS exploit prediction scores
entries.why: Daily rescored predictions, which is accuracy with a settleable outcome later.

entries.name: Have I Been Pwned
entries.why: Breach metadata only. Never route to the account-lookup path from a shared key.

groups.description: Company registries, beneficial ownership records, public procurement, and aid and spending transparency. These are the feeds that answer "who is this counterparty and what have they been paid", which is the question the demand register returns to most often. They are also the group where redistribution terms are most restrictive, because several registries fund themselves by selling the very data they publish. Candidates only, terms unread.

entries.name: Companies House API (UK)
entries.why: A national registry published openly with a real API and daily bulk files, which is the exception rather than the rule.

entries.name: Companies House Persons with Significant Control
entries.why: Beneficial ownership declared by the company itself, with known accuracy problems that only an anchor could quantify.

entries.name: Handelsregister (Germany)
entries.why: Recently opened to free retrieval, which is a licence change worth capturing precisely.

entries.name: KVK Business Register API (Netherlands)
entries.why: Charged per query, which makes cost reporting in the envelope load-bearing rather than decorative.

entries.name: Infogreffe (France)
entries.why: Commercial delivery of a public register, a recurring pattern in this file.

entries.name: INPI Registre National des Entreprises
entries.why: The open alternative to the commercial French delivery, which makes the pair a routing decision.

entries.name: SIRENE Establishment Database (France)
entries.why: Daily updates under an open licence, and the identifier spine for French business data.

entries.name: Registro Imprese (Italy)
entries.why: Paid access to a statutory register, so pass-through only.

entries.name: Bronnoysund Register Centre (Norway)
entries.why: Fully open, keyless, and updated continuously, which makes it the best promotion candidate in this file.

entries.name: Bolagsverket (Sweden)
entries.why: Charges for the same class of data Norway gives away, which is a useful contrast to record.

entries.name: CVR Danish Business Register
entries.why: Open data behind a registration, which separates licence from access again.

entries.name: YTJ Business Information System (Finland)
entries.why: Open API over company records with a documented update cycle.

entries.name: Australian Business Register
entries.why: Bulk extracts published regularly alongside a lookup API.

entries.name: New Zealand Business Number Register
entries.why: A national identifier scheme with an open API, useful as a join key.

entries.name: SEC Company Tickers and CIK Mapping
entries.why: The join file between filings and market data, updated without notice, which is a silent revision risk.

entries.name: CUSIP Issuer Reference
entries.why: A licensed identifier that many public datasets embed, which is a licence chain hazard worth recording before it bites.

entries.name: OpenFIGI
entries.why: An openly licensed instrument identifier, which is the alternative to the licensed ones above and directly relevant to H3.

entries.name: GLEIF Golden Copy Files
entries.why: Daily full files behind the GLEIF entry already registered, published under CC0.

entries.name: OpenSanctions
entries.why: Aggregates dozens of sanctions and PEP sources with per-source provenance already modelled, which is prior art worth studying closely.

entries.name: Open Ownership Register
entries.why: Beneficial ownership normalised across jurisdictions, the derivative half of the PSC entry.

entries.name: EU Beneficial Ownership Registers Index
entries.why: Access was narrowed after a court ruling, which is a legal availability change rather than a technical one.

entries.name: USAspending API
entries.why: The API behind the USAspending entry already registered, with quarterly restatements.

entries.name: Federal Procurement Data System Feed
entries.why: Contract actions published continuously, which is the primary USAspending aggregates.

entries.name: GSA Contract Pricing Data
entries.why: Negotiated prices that make procurement benchmarking possible.

entries.name: TED Europa API
entries.why: The machine interface for the TED entry already registered, with notice amendments.

entries.name: Open Contracting Data Standard Registry
entries.why: One schema adopted by dozens of national systems, which is the highest coverage per adapter in the whole registry.

entries.name: ProZorro (Ukraine)
entries.why: A fully open procurement system publishing every tender in real time.

entries.name: Compras.gov.br
entries.why: Federal purchasing data with an open API and high volume.

entries.name: CompraNet (Mexico)
entries.why: Published as bulk files under the national open data policy.

entries.name: Mercado Publico (Chile)
entries.why: A keyed API over every public tender, with a documented quota.

entries.name: Government e-Marketplace (India)
entries.why: Very large transaction volume with unclear reuse terms, so it waits for a reading.

entries.name: Find a Tender Service (UK)
entries.why: The post-Brexit successor to TED coverage for the UK, alongside the Contracts Finder entry already held.

entries.name: CanadaBuys Tender Notices
entries.why: Open bulk downloads with a stated refresh interval.

entries.name: AusTender
entries.why: Contract notices published with amendment histories intact.

entries.name: IATI Registry
entries.why: Thousands of publishers on one schema with per-publisher freshness, which is a completeness and punctuality dataset in its own right.

entries.name: OECD Creditor Reporting System
entries.why: The settled annual record that IATI's realtime reporting can be graded against.

entries.name: World Bank Projects and Operations API
entries.why: Project status changes and disbursements, which pairs with the debarred firms entry already registered.

entries.name: United Nations Global Marketplace
entries.why: UN system tenders in one place, with reuse terms that need checking.

entries.name: UK DevTracker
entries.why: A national derivative of IATI data, so its lag behind the registry is measurable.

entries.name: ForeignAssistance.gov
entries.why: US aid reporting that IATI also carries, giving a third view of the same transactions.

groups.description: Research repositories, bibliographic databases, and discipline archives. Science solved parts of the provenance problem long before anyone marketed it: a DOI is a content identifier, a data release is versioned, and a retraction is a published correction with a date. The value here is partly the data and partly the prior art. Candidates only, terms unread.

entries.name: DataCite REST API
entries.why: DOI metadata for datasets, including version relationships, which is lineage already expressed as a graph.

entries.name: ORCID Public API
entries.why: Persistent identifiers for people, which is the join key most bibliographic feeds lack.

entries.name: Research Organization Registry
entries.why: Released as versioned dumps under CC0, which makes it a clean reference dataset to route.

entries.name: Retraction Watch Database
entries.why: A correction feed for the scientific record, which is the same product shape the demand register keeps proposing.

entries.name: OpenAIRE Research Graph
entries.why: Links publications, datasets, and funding, and is explicitly a derivative of a dozen upstreams.

entries.name: CORE Aggregator
entries.why: Aggregates repository content at scale, which is a lineage depth test.

entries.name: BASE Bielefeld Academic Search Engine
entries.why: Non-commercial terms on an index that commercial tools quietly rely on.

entries.name: Unpaywall
entries.why: Open access status changes over time for the same DOI, which is a revision nobody tracks.

entries.name: OpenAlex Snapshot Release
entries.why: Monthly full dumps alongside the API already registered, so the same source has two very different freshness profiles.

entries.name: Scopus API
entries.why: Institutional licence only, so pass-through is the only lawful route.

entries.name: Web of Science API
entries.why: The other commercial index, listed so the boundary between free and licensed is explicit.

entries.name: Dimensions API
entries.why: Free for some research uses and paid otherwise, a use-class decision inside one source.

entries.name: Europe PMC RESTful API
entries.why: Full-text search with per-article licence fields, which is licence metadata done properly.

entries.name: bioRxiv API
entries.why: Preprint versions are numbered, so supersession is explicit in the identifier.

entries.name: medRxiv API
entries.why: Same mechanism in a field where a preprint can move policy before peer review.

entries.name: SSRN Listings
entries.why: Widely cited, commercially owned, and frequently scraped, which is a licence trap worth naming.

entries.name: Zenodo API
entries.why: Every record carries a licence field and a version DOI, which is the metadata we need and rarely get.

entries.name: Figshare API
entries.why: Another general repository with versioned items and per-item terms.

entries.name: Dryad API
entries.why: CC0 by policy, which makes it one of the few repositories with a single answer to the licence question.

entries.name: Open Science Framework API
entries.why: Preregistrations are timestamped commitments, which is an anchor for later claims.

entries.name: Harvard Dataverse
entries.why: Dataset versions are first-class and diffable, which is unusually close to what we do.

entries.name: ICPSR Data Archive
entries.why: Access tiers per study, so one source has several use classes at once.

entries.name: UK Data Service
entries.why: Registration-gated social science data, another pass-through case.

entries.name: GESIS Search
entries.why: German social science index with structured study metadata.

entries.name: CESSDA Data Catalogue
entries.why: A European federation of archives, so its records are derivative by construction.

entries.name: NCBI E-utilities
entries.why: One interface over two dozen databases with a documented rate limit, which exercises quota reporting in the envelope.

entries.name: NCBI Sequence Read Archive
entries.why: Submissions are amended after release, so the accession alone does not identify the bytes.

entries.name: Ensembl REST API
entries.why: Numbered releases every few months, which makes the version part of any correct answer.

entries.name: UniProt REST API
entries.why: Entries are curated and revised continuously with a published release cycle.

entries.name: RCSB Protein Data Bank
entries.why: Structures are occasionally obsoleted and replaced, which is supersession with a paper trail.

entries.name: ChEMBL
entries.why: Versioned releases with a share-alike style licence, which would propagate into envelopes.

entries.name: PubChem PUG REST
entries.why: Aggregates hundreds of depositor sources, each with its own terms, so the licence chain is genuinely deep.

entries.name: CAS Common Chemistry
entries.why: A small open window onto an otherwise commercial registry, which is a routing boundary.

entries.name: Materials Project API
entries.why: Computed rather than observed data, which the envelope should not describe as a measurement.

entries.name: NIST Standard Reference Data
entries.why: Reference values that other datasets are calibrated against, which makes it an anchor candidate.

entries.name: NIST Chemistry WebBook
entries.why: Widely used and rarely cited with a version, which is a provenance failure we can fix.

entries.name: Crossref Event Data
entries.why: A stream of references to works, which is a change feed over the literature.

entries.name: OpenCitations
entries.why: CC0 citation graph, the open counterpart to the commercial indexes above.

entries.name: DOAJ API
entries.why: Journal-level metadata that the article feeds join against, updated continuously.

entries.name: SciELO
entries.why: Latin American literature under-represented in the northern indexes, which is a completeness gap worth stating.

entries.name: J-STAGE (Japan)
entries.why: Japanese-language research similarly absent from the large aggregators.

entries.name: CNKI Public Index
entries.why: Subscription-gated, so it is recorded here only as a pass-through possibility.

entries.name: arXiv Bulk Data Access
entries.why: Bulk terms differ from the API terms on the same corpus, which is a licence subtlety worth encoding.

entries.name: NASA Astrophysics Data System
entries.why: Bibcodes are stable identifiers that predate DOIs, useful prior art for content addressing.

entries.name: INSPIRE-HEP
entries.why: Curated physics literature with an explicitly open API and CC0 metadata.

groups.description: Biomedical, scholarly, environmental, and public health feeds. This group carries the regulatory wedge (openFDA and friends) and the sources with the most interesting revision and completeness behaviour, because science corrects itself in public and on a schedule.

entries.name: openFDA
entries.why: MAUDE, 510(k), and recalls. The regulatory wedge, with duplicate reports to dedupe.

entries.name: ClinicalTrials.gov
entries.why: Trial records are amended continuously, with an explicit last-update timestamp.

entries.name: PubMed E-utilities
entries.why: Citation metadata at scale, with retractions as a correction-latency signal.

entries.name: PubMed Central Open Access subset
entries.why: Full text under per-article licences, which makes licence chaining concrete.

entries.name: Semantic Scholar
entries.why: Derivative of Crossref and others, so it is a second lineage test outside weather.

entries.name: OpenAlex
entries.why: Open scholarly graph, explicitly CC0, and a clean primary for citation lineage.

entries.name: Crossref
entries.why: DOI registration is the primary that OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar both derive from.

entries.name: arXiv API
entries.why: Versioned preprints, where revision is a first-class concept in the source itself.

entries.name: GBIF Global Biodiversity Information Facility
entries.why: Species occurrence records with per-dataset licences, so licence chaining is forced.

entries.name: NIH RePORTER
entries.why: Grant funding records, a completeness case broken out by institute.

entries.name: CDC Open Data
entries.why: Weekly series that backfill for weeks, the strongest revision-over-time example.

entries.name: CDC WONDER
entries.why: Mortality and natality with suppression rules that make completeness explicit.

entries.name: WHO Global Health Observatory
entries.why: International health indicators, a derivative of national statistical agencies.

entries.name: NPPES NPI Registry
entries.why: Provider identity, the join key for most US healthcare data work.

entries.name: RxNorm
entries.why: Drug terminology, the normalisation layer under any medication query.

entries.name: DailyMed
entries.why: Structured product labelling, updated when manufacturers file changes.

entries.name: USGS Water Services
entries.why: Values are flagged provisional then approved, so revisions are labelled by the source.

entries.name: AirNow
entries.why: Official US air quality, the primary that OpenAQ republishes.

entries.name: OpenAQ
entries.why: Aggregator of AirNow and others, a lineage pair with no licence complication.

entries.name: EPA ECHO
entries.why: Enforcement and compliance history, part of the regulatory wedge.

groups.description: Package registries and the services that index them. This group is the closest thing the registry has to a control group: releases are immutable once published, timestamps are exact, and cadence is high, so a freshness number here is unusually clean. It is also where lineage is obvious, since every aggregator names the registries it mirrors and lags them by hours.

entries.name: npm Registry
entries.why: A changes feed with sequence numbers, which gives an exact ordering to measure lag against.

entries.name: PyPI JSON API
entries.why: Per-project metadata with per-file hashes, so the content hash can be checked upstream.

entries.name: crates.io
entries.why: Publishes both an API and a nightly database dump, so live and cached can be compared.

entries.name: RubyGems
entries.why: Another registry with a versions index, cheap to poll and easy to diff.

entries.name: Packagist
entries.why: PHP ecosystem coverage, with a metadata mirror that lags the primary measurably.

entries.name: Maven Central
entries.why: Coordinates and checksums for the JVM, where artifacts are immutable by policy.

entries.name: NuGet
entries.why: A catalog resource designed for incremental consumption, which suits snapshotting.

entries.name: Go Module Proxy and Index
entries.why: The checksum database is a transparency log already, which is worth studying for Phase 2.

entries.name: Hex.pm
entries.why: Small enough to snapshot whole, which makes completeness trivially verifiable.

entries.name: CRAN via METACRAN
entries.why: CRAN archives old versions on a schedule, so availability changes without the data changing.

entries.name: conda-forge
entries.why: Channel index files republished on every build, a high-churn schema-stability case.

entries.name: Docker Hub Registry
entries.why: Tags are mutable while digests are not, which is the clearest example of why we hash.

entries.name: Homebrew Formulae API
entries.why: A single JSON file for the whole catalog, plus install analytics that revise daily.

entries.name: Debian Package Sources
entries.why: Per-suite indexes where the same package differs by suite, a completeness segment case.

entries.name: Arch Linux Package API
entries.why: A rolling release, so version churn is continuous rather than stepped.

entries.name: Repology
entries.why: Compares the same package across 300 distributions, which is our compare tool already built by somebody else, and therefore the obvious benchmark for ours.

entries.name: Libraries.io
entries.why: A derivative index across registries whose lag behind each primary is easy to measure.

entries.name: Ecosyste.ms
entries.why: Open infrastructure covering the same ground as Libraries.io, so the two can be compared.

entries.name: Open Source Insights (deps.dev)
entries.why: Dependency graphs with advisory joins, which links this group to the security feeds.

entries.name: endoflife.date
entries.why: Community-maintained support dates that change without notice, a correction-latency case.

groups.description: Orbital elements, planetary ephemerides, and astronomical archives. Astronomy solved provenance before anyone called it that: catalogs carry bibcodes, data releases are numbered, and alerts carry the instrument and the exposure that produced them. That makes this group less a source of customers than a source of prior art, plus a few feeds that decay fast enough to make freshness lag obvious. Orbital elements are stale within days, and everyone knows it.

entries.name: CelesTrak
entries.why: Two-line element sets whose accuracy decays measurably with age, which makes freshness lag a physical quantity rather than a convention.

entries.name: Space-Track.org
entries.why: The primary CelesTrak derives from, behind a per-account agreement that limits redistribution, so it can only ever be a pass-through source.

entries.name: JPL Horizons
entries.why: Ephemerides computed on request against a named kernel version, which is reproducibility with the method version already in the response.

entries.name: JPL CNEOS Close Approach Data
entries.why: Predictions that are revised as new observations arrive, with the solution date attached.

entries.name: Minor Planet Center
entries.why: Designations that change as objects are linked and merged, which is renaming as revision.

entries.name: NASA Exoplanet Archive
entries.why: Every parameter carries its reference, so per-row lineage exists without inference.

entries.name: Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes
entries.why: Observations are reprocessed with new calibrations, so the same exposure changes values.

entries.name: ESA Gaia Archive
entries.why: Numbered data releases that supersede without deleting, which is our snapshot model.

entries.name: SIMBAD
entries.why: An object database curated from the literature, updated daily, with edit dates exposed.

entries.name: VizieR
entries.why: Thousands of published catalogs behind one interface, each with its own citation.

entries.name: NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database
entries.why: Cross-identifications between catalogs, which is entity resolution with a paper trail.

entries.name: NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive
entries.why: Mission archives with explicit release versions, another reprocessing case.

entries.name: AAVSO Variable Star Index
entries.why: Amateur observations moderated before publication, a correction-latency case with humans.

entries.name: General Coordinates Network
entries.why: Transient alerts in seconds, then refined for hours, which is the fastest revise-in-public cycle in the registry and the sharpest correction-latency test available.

entries.name: Transient Name Server
entries.why: The naming authority that GCN reports resolve to, so the two can be checked against each other.

entries.name: ALeRCE Alert Broker
entries.why: A broker over survey alerts whose classifications change as more data arrives.

entries.name: NOIRLab Astro Data Archive
entries.why: Raw and reduced frames side by side, with proprietary periods that expire on a date.

entries.name: SDSS SkyServer
entries.why: Every data release stays queryable forever, which is as_of replay already implemented.

entries.name: ESA Space Weather Service Network
entries.why: A European read on the same solar events as NOAA SWPC, which makes disagreement visible.

entries.name: USGS Astrogeology Planetary Data
entries.why: Planetary basemaps versioned by product, slow enough to be a schema-stability baseline.

groups.description: Sports results and cultural heritage collections. They sit together because they are the two domains where the audience notices a stale answer instantly and where the licence position is least like the rest of the registry: sports data is aggressively commercial and heritage data is aggressively open. Routing correctly between them exercises the use-class machinery from both ends. Candidates only, terms unread.

entries.name: NFL Next Gen Stats Public Data
entries.why: League-published statistics with terms that restrict redistribution, which is the norm in this domain.

entries.name: NBA Stats Endpoints
entries.why: Widely used and never formally licensed, which is precisely the situation H3 forbids us from routing to on a guess.

entries.name: NHL Web API
entries.why: The successor to the endpoint behind the NHL entry already registered, which is a deprecation worth tracking.

entries.name: MLB Gameday Play-by-Play
entries.why: Pitch-level events published within seconds, which is the fastest publication clock in sports.

entries.name: Retrosheet
entries.why: A volunteer historical archive with explicit attribution terms and dated releases.

entries.name: Sportradar API
entries.why: The dominant commercial supplier, only ever routable with the customer's own contract.

entries.name: StatsBomb Open Data
entries.why: A commercial vendor's free research subset, which is a clean free-versus-pro routing case.

groups.description: Hydrology, water quality, and environmental monitoring networks. Gauge networks are the purest freshness problem in the registry: a station either reported in the last interval or it did not, there is no interpretation involved, and the failure mode during a flood is exactly when the data matters most. Several of these are also provisional-then-approved publishers, which gives revision behaviour a clean definition. Candidates only, terms unread.

entries.name: USGS NWIS Instantaneous Values
entries.why: Provisional readings later replaced by approved ones, with both retrievable, which is revision behaviour we do not have to infer.

entries.name: NOAA National Water Prediction Service

entries.name: NOAA National Water Model Output

entries.name: EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program

entries.name: AirNow API

entries.name: PurpleAir API

entries.name: EEA Industrial Emissions Portal

groups.description: National meteorological services and the model outputs they publish. Weather is the domain where a freshness claim is easiest to falsify: a forecast has a run time, an issue time, and a valid time, all three stated in the product itself, so lag is arithmetic rather than interpretation. It is also the domain with the widest spread of licences, from public domain to strictly commercial, which makes it a good proving ground for use-class routing. Candidates only.
